mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 7.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction permits (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a sharp contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-recession recovery phase (as indicated by rising industrial production), manufacturing output growth accelerates, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods during the post-recession recovery phase when INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO signal in this regime is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 0.25% signals aggressive monetary easing, which increases liquidity in financial markets and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS falls below 0.25%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 500,000 units signals a contraction in the housing market, which reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST falls below 500.0, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for INDPRO is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
